messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing (melting) point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice‑water equilibrium (slope ≈ –0.00007 K Pa⁻¹) gives:

\[
\Delta T \approx \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P
          \approx (-7\times10^{-5}\,\text{K Pa}^{-1})(10\,000-611.657)\,\text{Pa}
          \approx -0.66\,\text{K}
\]

So the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \approx 273.16\,\text{K} - 0.66\,\text{K}
                    \approx 272.5\,\text{K}
                    \approx -0.65^{\circ}\text{C}.
\]

**Answer:** About **–0.6 °C** (≈ 272.5 K).
